Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-11 14:00 UTC
Duration: 41 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Chen (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Arcturus - Head of ML Ops), Jon Park (Arcturus - Platform Eng), Priya Nair (Arcturus - Privacy & Compliance), Ethan Cole (Arcturus - CTO)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Samir Patel here from Redwood AE. Leah, you wanna say hi?
[00:07] Leah: Hi all, Leah Chen, solutions engineer. We'll go through the technical checklist and then dig into the bench plan.
[00:12] Marta: Marta here, thanks. We have Jon and Priya with me, and Ethan should join in a minute.
[00:20] Jon: Hey all.
[00:22] Priya: Hi.
[00:25] Ethan: Sorry for the slight delay, CTO duty called.
[00:29] Samir: No worries. Agenda: quick renewal posture, the EU private edge ask, latency SLOs and bench plan, security/KMS questions, and next steps. Does that cover it?
[00:38] Ethan: Yep, that's it. We want to confirm if the pilot is feasible and what the expected uplift will be. Also need to understand the SLA change if we go to private.
[00:48] Marta: To add, our procurement has asked about a firm 95th percentile target for EU region—so we need bench numbers.
[00:56] Leah: Great. From a tech perspective, we want to run two things: a throughput sweep to confirm burst capacity and a latency tail test for your prompt mixes. We'll instrument 95th and 99th percentiles, and capture tokens/sec and KV cache hit behavior.
[01:12] Jon: Quick Q — when you say KV cache, we've had previous vendors that called it K-V cash or similar, so just making sure we measure warm cache vs cold?
[01:21] Leah: Yes warm vs cold. We'll simulate both prefix cache warmups to reflect your traffic. Also, we'll include a prefix caching policy to match your traffic patterns.
[01:29] Priya: From security side, the three items I need are KMS integration details, audit log retention, and how keys are rotated or whether HSM is supported.
[01:40] Samir: Totally. We can share our KMS integration guide; Redwood supports customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and HSM for private deployments. We'll include rotation and BYOK notes.
[01:50] Ethan: If we go private, does Redwood's monitoring still push to our Datadog or is it isolated?
[01:57] Leah: You can configure exporters to your monitoring stack. For Private we provide a sidecar that emits metrics and traces to your endpoint. We'll document the exact metrics and sample rate.
[02:07] Marta: Great. On pricing — procurement is pushing for a 24-month term but they'll accept 12 if the upfront discount is compelling. What's the usual tradeoff?
[02:18] Samir: Typically more aggressive unit discounts on 24 months and guaranteed reserved capacity. For 12 months we can do a modest discount but we need to quantify the unit economics. I'll put a few scenarios in the pricing sheet.
[02:29] Jon: Do you have examples of billing cadence for burst? Like how do you measure burst credit usage?
[02:36] Leah: We have a burst pool mechanism for Dedicated and Private where short spikes borrow from a burst bucket. We charge based on provisioned tokens and overage at a pre-agreed rate. We'll put that in the sheet.
[02:45] Priya: On data residency, if we store logs for 90 days, can we restrict retention to EU-only?
[02:51] Samir: Yes, for Private you control retention policies; for Hosted we can support tenant regioning and restrict where logs are persisted. We'll add specifics in the KMS/SOC artifact.
[02:59] Marta: OK, can we pivot to the bench day logistics? We'd like to run this against our staging traffic shape — about 600 rps peak with median sequences of 120 tokens and some long tail at 800 tokens.
[03:13] Leah: That's perfect — we'll reproduce that shape. Our bench will include synthetic workload that mirrors those distributions. We'll also capture 95th p99.9 to show tail.
[03:23] Ethan: How long do you need to run the bench to get representative numbers?
[03:27] Leah: I'd say a full hourly sweep running increasing load for 45–60 minutes plus a separate cold-start series. That'll align with your traffic spikes.
[03:34] Jon: Are there any infra pre-reqs for the EU VPC peering? Firewall rules, static egress IPs?
[03:40] Samir: We'll provide the minimal allowlist and peering steps. For private we can also support a direct connect equivalent — we'll detail options.
[03:46] Marta: Procurement also cares about an SLA uplift if we move to private — like lower latency SLOs and a higher uptime SLA. Is that negotiable?
[03:55] Samir: For Private we can commit to more stringent latency targets and higher SLAs backed by operational runbooks. The specifics depend on the committed capacity tier. Again, I'll surface options in the pricing doc.
[04:06] Leah: Tech note: some of the low-latency gains come from quantization and kernel selection. We'll capture model variants and quantization profiles in the bench to show tradeoffs in latency vs quality.
[04:18] Jon: Will model quality change if we quantize? We can't degrade customer-facing outputs beyond x perplexity.
[04:24] Leah: We'll show ROUGE/BLEU-style comparisons for your eval prompts and track regression thresholds. If quality drops beyond your tolerance we can switch to less aggressive quantization or a larger model variant.
[04:35] Marta: Any vendor comparators? We tried CloudPrompt and VertexEdge; they hit good throughput but had worse tail latency during prefix-heavy traffic.
[04:44] Samir: That's helpful context. We'll design the bench to highlight tail behavior under prefix cache stress so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[04:52] Ethan: Security — is Redwood able to provide SOC2 or ISO excerpts for private deployments?
[04:57] Samir: Yes, we can provide SOC2 Type II summary and ISO attestation docs, plus a private-deploy security checklist. We'll attach those when we send the KMS note.
[05:07] Priya: Also need legal to review data processing addendum — will you share a template?
[05:12] Samir: Yep, we'll share an NDA/DPA template and procurement checklist.
[05:16] Marta: On timeline, procurement is pushing for a signed amendment within the next 30 days if the bench goes well. Is that realistic?
[05:23] Samir: If bench passes and security sign-off is okay, 30 days is achievable. We'll aim for procurement call week of Feb 25.
[05:30] Leah: Quick technical question from Jon — can we allocate a pre-warmed KV cache so your first N requests don't hit the slow path?
[05:37] Jon: Yes that's important for customer-facing latency.
[05:39] Leah: We can pre-warm prefixes and script the warmup during bench. That will be included.
[05:45] Marta: Pricing again — can you show a blended per-token rate including reserved and burst amortized?
[05:51] Samir: Yes, we'll include blended scenarios and show the math with examples matched to your 600 rps peak.
[05:57] Ethan: One small ask — we want a dedicated contact for day-of bench support with SSH access to the runner to iterate quickly.
[06:03] Samir: Leah will be the on-call SE for the bench. I'll be the commercial lead. Leah: sounds good.
[06:09] Leah: I'll join with the bench scripts and the reproducible runbook. We'll also give you the Docker image we use for the client runner.
[06:16] Jon: Any risk of data leaking to other tenants during the bench?
[06:20] Leah: No, bench will run in an isolated tenant with strict tenant isolation. For Private there's physical isolation too.
[06:26] Priya: About logs — we need to ensure PII is scrubbed from retention. Can we do field-level filtering?
[06:33] Samir: Yes, there are redaction hooks and configurable retention rules. We'll document the supported filters.
[06:39] Martha: (laughs) Marta, not Martha — sorry, slip.
[06:43] Samir: No worries.
[06:45] [07:12] -- 7-minute marker -- more technical back-and-forth on queueing and autoscaler thresholds. --
[07:13] Jon: For autoscaler thresholds, what's the smoothing window? If we set it too aggressive, warmups might cause thrash.
[07:20] Leah: Default smoothing is 60s with a cooldown of 120s; we'll tune to your traffic shape during bench.
[07:28] Jon: Perfect.
[07:30] [12:01] Leah: (runs through bench plan) Step 1: cold-start runs; Step 2: steady ramp to 600 rps; Step 3: 800 token long-tail stress; Step 4: cache-warmup validation; Step 5: failover to secondary region test.
[12:18] Marta: For failover, how quickly do you route to a secondary? We need graceful degradation so user requests don't error during a primary outage.
[12:25] Leah: We have a traffic routing policy: multi-tier, first try local private node, then regional fallback, finally hosted fallback. We can tune TTLs to your needs. We'll capture failover latency in the bench.
[12:36] Ethan: Are there cost implications for keeping a hot standby in EU?
[12:39] Samir: Yes, hot standby is more costly; we can present a warm standby option with faster spin-up and lower cost. Details in price scenarios.
[12:47] Priya: For compliance, do you support key-splitting or dual-control for KMS?
[12:52] Samir: We support customer-managed keys and can support HSM-backed keys with dual-control workflows in private deployments. We'll include sample architecture.
[12:59] [25:00] -- mid call preparation and small side conversation about dates --
[25:05] Samir: Quick recap: Leah runs bench, Samir sends pricing and docs, Arcturus provides network and KMS constraints, bench week of Feb 23. Any blockers?
[25:16] Marta: If Leah can show a 95th percentile under 120ms for our staging shape, procurement will go to legal. That's the threshold.
[25:25] Leah: We'll try to achieve that; if not, we'll show alternate model/quantization options to reach it.
[25:31] Jon: Also want the reproducible script so we can rerun locally.
[25:35] Leah: Yes, we'll give the script and a dockerized runner.
[25:39] Priya: I'll compile the KMS constraints and send them by Monday.
[25:43] Ethan: Sounds good.
[25:46] Samir: Anything else?
[25:48] Marta: No, thanks.
[25:50] Samir: Ok we'll follow up with the pricing sheet and security artifacts today, Leah will post the bench runbook and we will lock the bench day. Follow-up procurement touchpoint week of Feb 25.
[25:59] [39:30] Closing remarks and brief off-topic chat about weekend plans.
[39:40] Samir: Thank you everyone. We'll email action items and calendar invites.
[39:45] Marta: Thanks, talk soon.
[39:48] Jon: Bye.
[39:50] Priya: Bye.
[39:52] Ethan: Bye.
